correctness.rationale: PASS. For left H=A with <x,y>=xy*, the singleton Parseval identity xs* s x*=xx* for every x is equivalent (take x=1) to s*s=1. On A^k, the diagonal vector produces sum_{i,j}x_i s_i* s_j x_j*, equal to sum_i x_i x_i* for every x iff s_i*s_j=delta_ij; polarization with x_i=1 and x_j=1,i proves off-diagonal zero. These relations also explicitly generate A^k by a=sum_i x_i s_i*. Two orthogonal isometries v,w give s_j=v^(j-1)w, which are mutually orthogonal isometries for all finite k; absence of two forces maximal k=1. For A=B(l2), the basis maps s_j e_n=e_{2^(j-1)(2n-1)} are pairwise range-orthogonal and 1 is a complete wandering vector. The published Theorem 5.3 proof fails because its sum of nonzero pairwise orthogonal positive projections can remain <=1 for every finite k. This is a universal algebraic proof, not inference from finite checks.
